subject: Change order: add burst GPU capacity + price adjustment (BrightLayer)
messages:
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@brightlayer.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightlayer.com>, BrightLayer Contracts <contracts@brightlayer.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Change order request: temporary burst capacity + price revision

Hannah —

Quick note from procurement: our usage spiked unexpectedly this week during a clinical data ingest test. We need to add burst GPU capacity (~40 x T4-equivalent hours/day for the next 30 days) and would like a short-term price adjustment for the additional capacity.

Can Redwood send a change order (Order Form amendment) with:
- line item for "Burst GPU capacity" (hours + hourly rate)
- a 30-day term for the burst (start date April 6)
- an explicit statement that standard SLA and data handling terms remain in effect

We also need to understand whether this requires a PO or if DocuSign will suffice for our finance team. If you can attach a draft today, I can share with our legal.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Cole
Senior Procurement Manager, BrightLayer Health
E: evan.cole@brightlayer.com
T: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightlayer.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Change order request: temporary burst capacity + price revision

Evan —

Thanks for the heads-up. I've drafted a change order and a redlined Order Form that adds a "Burst GPU" line item and sets a 30-day burst period. I'm attaching the initial draft and the redline for your legal team to review. Key points included:

- Burst capacity: 40 T4-equivalent GPU-hours/day, billed hourly as a separate line item
- Burst term: 30 days (auto-expire unless mutually extended)
- One-time provisioning fee (listed separately)
- Billing: billed monthly in arrears; we can accept a PO but DocuSign signature will also work to trigger provisioning

Attachment stubs: BrightLayer_CO_Draft_v1.pdf; Redline_OrderForm_20260405.docx

If you want any fast concessions (for example, a small introductory credit), let me know and I can run pricing approval with my finance lead.

I'll loop in legal and pricing internally — copying Alex here for completeness.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

--
Redwood Inference — Helping teams run LLM inference reliably

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quick redline notes for BrightLayer CO

Hannah —

I pulled the draft. A few suggested edits from legal/procurement POV before we send v2:

1) Termination/renewal language — make the burst explicitly non-renewing unless both parties sign an extension; avoids ambiguous auto-renew clauses.
2) Audit logs & retention — BrightLayer asked about logs in their note; propose a 90-day audit log retention commit for any burst requests and include a sentence that audit logs related to burst activity will be available on request.
3) Pricing tier cap — add a cap on total burst spend (e.g., $25k cap) so we don't accidentally exceed an expected spend. If customer wants higher, we escalate to sales for a committed capacity quote.
4) Billing cadence — default to monthly in arrears; if customer insists on PO-based billing, add a clause that provisioning will wait for PO receipt if they choose that path.
5) SOW attachment — confirm the SOW reference points to the production model list (to avoid PLM mismatch).

Marcus: any concerns on the provisioning side or SLA exceptions for burst nodes (preemptible vs dedicated)?

If all good, I'll mark up the document and return to you by EOD.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightlayer.com>, BrightLayer Contracts <contracts@brightlayer.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Updated change order (v2) and next steps

Evan —

Attached is change order v2 (PDF) and a redline that reflects our legal comments:
- Burst term is non-renewing unless extended in writing
- We included a $25,000 spend cap for the 30-day burst (helps control surprise spend)
- Audit log retention: 90 days for burst-related logs; requestable exports included
- Billing: monthly in arrears; DocuSign signature will trigger provisioning unless you prefer we wait for a PO

DocuSign link to sign (for your convenience): https://www.docusign.com/sign/EXAMPLE/BRIGHT-CO

If you prefer, we can also walk through the changes on a 15-minute call today. Once signed we can provision burst capacity on the requested start date (April 6) and invoice per the Order Form.

Thanks — please let me know if your legal team redlines further.

Best,
Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightLayer_CO_Draft_v2.pdf, Redline_OrderForm_20260405.docx

From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@brightlayer.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightlayer.com>, BrightLayer Contracts <contracts@brightlayer.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Updated change order (v2) and next steps

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for accommodating our burst window. Our legal reviewed the draft and has two minor asks:

1) Data residency note — can we add an explicit sentence that processing for the burst will remain in US regions (we can't accept cross-border processing for this data set).
2) Billing cadence — they prefer to issue a PO and have billing monthly; they'd like provisioning to start on signature if possible but are happy to have the PO issued in parallel.

If you accept those two tweaks, we can sign via DocuSign today and I'll route a PO through finance. We appreciate the $25k cap — that helps get approval faster.

We'll countersign pending the added residency sentence.

Regards,
Evan
Senior Procurement Manager, BrightLayer Health
